immediate_action_required: Call 112 (ERSS) or reach the nearest designated/empanelled hospital immediately
reporting_requirement: Police authentication on an integrated digital system is required to continue treatment beyond initial stabilisation
medical_action_required: Cashless trauma/polytrauma care at a designated hospital
police_action: Coordinates with hospital for police authentication
insurer_action: Not applicable - Fund-financed, not an insurance claim against a specific insurer
benefit_description: Cashless treatment up to Rs 1,50,000 per victim per accident, for hospitalisation up to 7 days from the date of the accident
benefit_amount: Rs 1,50,000 per victim, per accident
eligibility_conditions: Any victim of a road accident caused by a motor vehicle on any category of road, regardless of fault, insurance status, or nationality

medical_action_required: Stabilisation treatment for up to 24 hours
benefit_description: Stabilisation treatment covered for up to 24 hours in non-life-threatening cases before further authorisation review
benefit_amount: within the overall Rs 1,50,000 / 7-day cap
eligibility_conditions: Case classified as non-life-threatening by the treating hospital

immediate_action_required: Reach a PM RAHAT-designated hospital immediately
medical_action_required: Stabilisation treatment for up to 48 hours
benefit_description: Stabilisation treatment covered for up to 48 hours in life-threatening cases before further authorisation review
benefit_amount: within the overall Rs 1,50,000 / 7-day cap
eligibility_conditions: Case classified as life-threatening by the treating hospital

reporting_requirement: Not a substitute for the eventual FIR/police report needed for other claims
medical_action_required: ERSS operator guides caller to the nearest designated hospital and can dispatch an ambulance
police_action: Coordinates dispatch with police and hospitals
benefit_description: Immediate guidance to the nearest designated hospital and ambulance dispatch coordination
benefit_amount: not applicable (coordination service, not a monetary benefit)
eligibility_conditions: Any road accident victim, Good Samaritan (Rah-Veer), or bystander at the accident site

medical_action_required: Hospitals reimbursed from this account for treating victims where the at-fault vehicle is insured
insurer_action: General Insurance Council administers reimbursement under the Motor Vehicle Accident Fund Trust
benefit_description: Funds hospital reimbursement for golden-hour cashless treatment where the vehicle involved is insured
benefit_amount: not applicable (funding mechanism, not a direct victim benefit)
eligibility_conditions: Accident involved an insured motor vehicle

medical_action_required: Hospitals reimbursed from this account for treating victims where the at-fault vehicle is uninsured or involved in a hit-and-run
insurer_action: General Insurance Council administers reimbursement under the Motor Vehicle Accident Fund Trust
benefit_description: Funds hospital reimbursement for golden-hour cashless treatment where the vehicle is uninsured or untraced
benefit_amount: not applicable (funding mechanism, not a direct victim benefit)
eligibility_conditions: Accident involved an uninsured vehicle, or the vehicle could not be traced (hit-and-run)

insurer_action: General Insurance Council administers this dedicated account under the Motor Vehicle Accident Fund Trust
benefit_description: Separate account within the Motor Vehicle Accident Fund specifically financing the Hit and Run Compensation Scheme payouts (distinct from golden-hour treatment reimbursement)
benefit_amount: funds the fixed hit-and-run compensation amounts (see RELIEF_HITRUN_DEATH / RELIEF_HITRUN_GRIEVOUS_INJURY)
eligibility_conditions: Claim approved under the Hit and Run Compensation Scheme, 2022

immediate_action_required: File FIR promptly with police describing the untraced vehicle
reporting_requirement: FIR mandatory, since the vehicle cannot be traced for a direct insurance claim
police_action: Police investigation to confirm the vehicle could not be identified/traced
insurer_action: Not applicable - Scheme-funded via Motor Vehicle Accident Fund, not an insurers own claim
benefit_description: Fixed compensation of Rs 2,00,000 to the legal heirs where death results from an accident caused by an unidentified/untraced motor vehicle
eligibility_conditions: Vehicle causing the accident could not be identified or traced; death resulted from the accident

immediate_action_required: File FIR promptly with police describing the untraced vehicle
medical_action_required: Medical treatment and documentation of grievous hurt
police_action: Police investigation to confirm the vehicle could not be identified/traced
insurer_action: Not applicable - Scheme-funded, not an insurers own claim
benefit_description: Fixed compensation of Rs 50,000 for grievous hurt caused by an unidentified/untraced motor vehicle
eligibility_conditions: Vehicle causing the accident could not be identified or traced; injury classified as grievous hurt

immediate_action_required: Voluntarily render emergency assistance in good faith without expectation of reward
reporting_requirement: No obligation to report unless the bystander chooses to
medical_action_required: Assist the victim or facilitate their transfer to a hospital
police_action: No obligation to disclose identity unless willing
benefit_description: Protection from civil/criminal liability for good-faith emergency assistance; no obligation to act as a witness unless willing
benefit_amount: not a monetary benefit
eligibility_conditions: Assistance was rendered voluntarily, in good faith, without expectation of payment

insurer_action: Insurer/owner contests or settles the claim before the Tribunal
benefit_description: Full fault-based compensation computed by the MACT applying the multiplier method and standardised conventional heads
benefit_amount: case-specific, no fixed cap
eligibility_conditions: Claimant proves negligence/fault; not available in combination with a Section 163A structured claim for the same accident

insurer_action: Insurer pays per the structured formula without a full fault inquiry
benefit_description: Faster, structured-formula compensation without the need to prove fault/negligence in detail
benefit_amount: per the Second Schedule structured formula (amounts NOT_VERIFIED in this session)
eligibility_conditions: Claimant opts for this route instead of Section 166; mutually exclusive per Deepal Girishbhai Soni v. United India Insurance Co.

insurer_action: Insurer pays the fixed no-fault amount pending the final award
benefit_description: Fixed interim compensation payable without proof of fault or negligence, adjustable against the final MACT award
benefit_amount: amount NOT_VERIFIED against a current primary source this session
eligibility_conditions: Available regardless of who was at fault; does not require establishing wrongful act, neglect or default

insurer_action: Insurer of the at-fault vehicle indemnifies the third-party victim/claimant
benefit_description: Compensation for injury, death, or property damage caused to a third party by the insured vehicle
benefit_amount: per policy terms and/or MACT award
eligibility_conditions: Valid third-party insurance in force on the at-fault vehicle at the time of the accident

insurer_action: Insurer assesses and settles damage to the policyholders own vehicle
benefit_description: Reimbursement/repair coverage for damage to the insureds own vehicle, subject to policy terms and any comprehensive/own-damage add-on
benefit_amount: per policy terms (own-damage cover is optional, unlike third-party cover)
eligibility_conditions: Comprehensive or own-damage policy in force; not covered under the mandatory third-party-only minimum required by Section 146

insurer_action: Insurer of the at-fault vehicle indemnifies third-party property damage, subject to a statutory cap for property-only claims
benefit_description: Compensation for damage to third-party property (e.g. another vehicle, a structure) caused by the insured vehicle
benefit_amount: subject to a statutory cap on property-damage-only third-party liability (exact current cap NOT_VERIFIED)
eligibility_conditions: Valid third-party insurance in force on the at-fault vehicle

benefit_description: Compensation computed across the structured checklist of heads from Raj Kumar v. Ajay Kumar (medical expenses, loss of earnings during treatment, loss of future earning capacity, pain and suffering, loss of amenities/marriage prospects)
benefit_amount: case-specific, based on functional (not merely medical) disability per Mallikarjun v. Divisional Manager, NIC Ltd.
eligibility_conditions: Permanent disability established by medical evidence; compensation based on functional impact on the claimants occupation, not just the medical disability percentage

benefit_description: Fixed conventional-head compensation for spousal, parental, and filial consortium, per Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Nanuram
benefit_amount: fixed conventional amount, periodically revised by the Supreme Court (exact current figure NOT_VERIFIED)
eligibility_conditions: Claimant is a spouse, parent, or child of the deceased

benefit_description: Fixed conventional-head amount for funeral expenses, per National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi
benefit_amount: fixed conventional amount, periodically revised by the Supreme Court (exact current figure NOT_VERIFIED)
eligibility_conditions: Death resulted from the accident

benefit_description: Fixed conventional-head amount for loss of estate, per National Insurance Co. Ltd. v. Pranay Sethi
benefit_amount: fixed conventional amount, periodically revised by the Supreme Court (exact current figure NOT_VERIFIED)
eligibility_conditions: Death resulted from the accident

benefit_description: Addition to the deceaseds assessed income (40% up to age 40, tapering with age) before applying the multiplier, per Pranay Sethi
benefit_amount: percentage addition to income, not a fixed sum
eligibility_conditions: Applies even to self-employed or fixed-income deceased, per the standardisation in Pranay Sethi

benefit_description: Compensation computed using notional income and a multiplier framework specific to child/minor victims, per Kishan Gopal v. Lala
benefit_amount: case-specific, using notional income given the absence of an actual earning history
eligibility_conditions: Deceased was a minor at the time of death

immediate_action_required: Seek immediate medical attention; report to police
reporting_requirement: FIR recommended for both MACT claim and insurance purposes
medical_action_required: Emergency treatment, potentially via the PM RAHAT golden-hour scheme regardless of fault
police_action: Investigation to establish which vehicle/driver was at fault
insurer_action: Insurer of the at-fault vehicle indemnifies the pedestrian as a third party
benefit_description: Third-party compensation via the at-fault vehicles insurer, and/or MACT claim; golden-hour cashless treatment is available regardless of fault determination
benefit_amount: per policy/MACT award for liability compensation; Rs 1,50,000 cap for the separate golden-hour treatment benefit
eligibility_conditions: Pedestrian injured/killed by a motor vehicle in a public place

reporting_requirement: FIR recommended to establish the vehicle was uninsured
medical_action_required: Golden-hour treatment still available regardless of the vehicles insurance status
police_action: Investigation to confirm the vehicle was uninsured at the time of accident
insurer_action: No insurer of record for the at-fault vehicle; Motor Vehicle Accident Fund (Uninsured Vehicles account) steps in for treatment reimbursement
benefit_description: Golden-hour treatment reimbursed via the Funds Uninsured Vehicles account; victim may still pursue a MACT claim directly against the uninsured owner/driver
benefit_amount: Rs 1,50,000 cap for golden-hour treatment; MACT award amount is case-specific
eligibility_conditions: Vehicle causing the accident was being used without valid insurance

immediate_action_required: Ask staff to confirm PM RAHAT/empanelment status; request escalation within the hospital
benefit_description: If a designated/empanelled hospital refuses treatment under the scheme, or pre-authorisation is stuck, the matter can be escalated to the National Health Authority or via an RTI request for scheme records
benefit_amount: not a monetary benefit (grievance/escalation pathway)
eligibility_conditions: Hospital is designated/empanelled under the scheme but is refusing or delaying cashless treatment

benefit_description: Not a direct victim benefit - this row documents that the golden-hour cashless treatment schemes actual notification was compelled by Supreme Court orders in S. Rajaseekaran v. Union of India (2025 INSC 45, 8 January 2025), which found the decades-long delay in framing a Section 162 scheme a breach of Article 21 (right to life)
benefit_amount: not applicable
eligibility_conditions: Legal/contextual record only - links the PM RAHAT scheme to its enforcement history

benefit_description: Before the nationwide May 2025 notification, a cashless-treatment pilot scheme operated in a smaller set of States (reported as six States, including Uttar Pradesh, as of December 2024); any State-specific top-up terms predating the national scheme are NOT_VERIFIED and superseded by the national scheme
benefit_amount: varies by State pilot; not confirmed in this session
eligibility_conditions: Accident occurred in a State that ran an earlier pilot scheme, before nationwide PM RAHAT coverage began

benefit_description: Where more than one vehicle/driver contributed to the accident, the Tribunal apportions liability and compensation between the at-fault parties insurers according to their relative degree of fault
benefit_amount: case-specific apportionment; no fixed formula in the Act itself
eligibility_conditions: Accident involved contributory negligence by more than one driver/vehicle

immediate_action_required: Seek treatment at a hospital empanelled under Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY, which commonly overlaps with PM RAHAT-designated hospitals
medical_action_required: Treatment delivered through the existing PM-JAY hospital network, administered by the National Health Authority
benefit_description: The National Health Authority (NHA), which also implements Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY, is the implementing agency for PM RAHAT, using the same hospital empanelment infrastructure
benefit_amount: not applicable (infrastructure/administration note, not a separate benefit amount)
eligibility_conditions: Treatment sought at a hospital empanelled under both PM-JAY and PM RAHAT

benefit_description: Documents the statutory definition: golden hour means the one hour following a traumatic injury, during which the likelihood of preventing death through prompt medical care is the highest, as defined in Section 2(12-A) of the MV Act
benefit_amount: not applicable (definitional record, not a benefit)
eligibility_conditions: Legal/definitional record only
